cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Event sourcing stores every change as an immutable event (OrderPlaced, PaymentReceived) in an append-only log and rebuilds state by replaying them, giving a full audit trail and time travel. CQRS splits the write model from read models so each is optimized separately.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Combined: a command is validated and appends an event; projections update read views; queries read the views, so reads are eventually consistent. Snapshots keep replay fast. The two ideas are independent. Worth it for audit-heavy domains, diverging read and write patterns, or naturally event-shaped domains.

questions.q: After a command, can the user immediately read their change?
questions.a: Not necessarily. The read model is updated afterward by a projection, so reads are briefly stale.
No. They are commonly combined but are independent decisions.
To avoid replaying the entire event history to rebuild current state.
